label: token c held in memory: early-c original phase and approach to c output in copy
explanation: A token-specific feature for the letter c. In the copy phase (and at <DEL>) it ramps up over the 1-3 steps before c is due to be output, peaks on the step that outputs c (97.6% of out_tok==c steps are active), and stays on for the step where c is fed back as input; then it decays. In the original phase it fires only when c was one of the first ~3 tokens, starting about 3 steps after c (t>=3), and stays weakly active through <DEL>. Magnitude is highest for repeated c (top examples are c c c ... sequences, near max right after <DEL> when the outputs are c). It is essentially silent when c is not in the sequence (only weak, low-quartile noise), never fires at t<2, and does not fire on c input in the original phase when c comes late. Leftover errors come from fuzzy ramp onset/offset timing.
